channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Why Saudi Arabia’s Aim of Defeating Yemen’s Houthis Is a Tall Order
item.description: After four years of relative calm, the war pitting Yemen’s Houthi militia against the country’s internationally recognized government and its backer Saudi Arabia is back on. Announcing the start of a full-scale military campaign against the Houthis, the Saudi-led coalition supporting government forces said on social media on Oct. 4 that the goal is to “eliminate” the group.
item.dc:creator: Veena Ali-Khan and Paul Wallace

item.title: Deadly Attacks on Saudi Arabia Raise Wider War Risks
item.description: Saudi Arabia suffered its deadliest strikes since the Iran war began as Houthi militants repeatedly targeted airports across the kingdom, killing at least 14 people and wounding hundreds at the weekend. The Saudi-led military coalition said it intercepted missiles and drones aimed at the kingdom overnight. Bloomberg's Abeer Abu Omar reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Deadly Houthi Attacks on Saudi Arabia; EU Caps Chinese Hybrid Car Imports
item.description:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from Brussels, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. And we'll tell you what matters for investors in Europe, giving you insight before trading begins.
On today's show, attacks over the weekend in Saudi Arabia in which 13 people were killed risk widening the conflict in the Middle East. An American was among those killed on Saturday, raising pressure for US President Donald Trump to act.
Oil extended losses as traders assessed President Trump's announcement of an 'energy ceasefire' between Russia and Ukraine.
And the EU has announced a cap of 350,000 on imports of Chinese hybrid cars following talks between trade chief Maroš Šefčovič and Chinese Commerce Minister Wang Wentao.
Today's guest: Ana Paula Assis, IBM, Senior Vice President & Chair, EMEA & APAC & François Provost, Renault, CEO. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Britain’s Mansion Tax Shows the Difficulty of Targeting Wealth
item.description: Critics of wealth taxes say they are fiendishly difficult to administer and politically perilous. Britain’s Labour government was hoping to avoid both pitfalls when it came up with a lighter alternative, but the so-called mansion tax is still at risk of a messy start.
item.dc:creator: Tom Rees

item.title: Trump’s Russia Diesel Deal Will Aid Putin’s War, Europe Warns
item.description: European officials cautioned that President Donald Trump’s deal to increase Russia’s diesel sales will boost Moscow’s war effort in Ukraine, pressing for more US sanctions instead.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Palasciano and Max Ramsay

item.title: Saudis Say New Missiles Intercepted After Deadly Airport Attacks
item.description: The Saudi-led military coalition fighting the Houthis said it intercepted missiles and drones aimed at the kingdom overnight, including areas that are home to some of Saudi Arabia’s key oil and gas facilities.
item.dc:creator: Christine Burke

item.title: McNally: Oil Market Underappreciates Geopolitical Risk
item.description: Oil extended declines as traders weigh President Donald Trump's claim of an "energy ceasefire" between Russia and Ukraine. This comes after hostilities escalated across the Middle East, with strikes by Houthis on Saudi Arabia’s Riyadh airport. Bob McNally, President and Founder of Rapidan Energy Group and Former White House energy advisor spoke to Bloomberg’s Abeer Abu Omar on Horizons Middle East and Africa from Riyadh on the impact of the various geopolitical situations on the oil market. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nationalizing English Water Firms Could Cost £105 Billion
item.description: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s push for greater control of England’s troubled water industry could come with a hefty price tag of about £105 billion, according to a new industry-commissioned analysis.
item.dc:creator: Jessica Shankleman

item.title: India's CJP Renews Call for Poll Body Chief to Quit
item.description: After a weekend of mass detentions and heavy security in Delhi, opposition parties plan to submit a memorandum to India's chief justice demanding an end to alleged electoral manipulation, a halt to voter-roll revisions and the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: What Houthi Airport Attacks Mean for Oil Market, Trump
item.description: Saudi Arabia’s main airport came under renewed attack from Houthi rebels. Bloomberg journalists and Jean-Loup Samaan, senior research fellow at the Middle East Institute of the National University of Singapore, discuss. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: China Sanctions Officials of Taiwan’s Partners for First Time
item.description: China imposed sanctions on officials from Paraguay and Belize over their support for Taiwan, the first time Beijing has used such moves against diplomatic partners of the self-ruled island.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Zelenskyy Risks Rupture with Trump as Kyiv Resists US Pressure
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is on a collision course with President Donald Trump, who is increasingly looking at Kyiv’s battle against Russia primarily through the lens of energy prices ahead of US midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Aliaksandr Kudrytski, Natalia Drozdiak and Alberto Nardelli

item.title: India’s Delhi Braces for More Protests After Mass Detentions
item.description: India is bracing for a third straight day of tensions in its capital, with opposition parties on Monday planning a march to the Supreme Court and a youth-led movement pressing ahead with protests over a contentious revision of voter rolls.
item.dc:creator: Atul Dev and Asmi Bhatia

item.title: US Judge Halts Taxpayer-Funded TV Ads Lauding Trump for Now
item.description: A federal judge in New York ordered the Trump administration to stop for now running taxpayer-funded television ads lauding the president and to halt any payments of public money related to airing them as legal challenges move ahead.
item.dc:creator: Zoe Tillman

item.title: North Korea Fires Missiles After Border Breach Warning
item.description: North Korea fired multiple ballistic missiles off its east coast Monday, days after warning Seoul of retaliation if its territory were violated.
item.dc:creator: Soo-Hyang Choi

item.title: Ruling Australian Labor Party Regains Poll Lead on Tepid Support
item.description: Australia’s ruling Labor party has regained the lead in a national poll that showed all of the major political groupings remain unpopular with voters, as no party managed to breach 30%.
item.dc:creator: James Mayger

item.title: Mamdani Says New York Will Investigate ICE Shooting in the City
item.description: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said that the city would investigate the Immigration and Customs Enforcement shooting that left a man wounded on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: María Paula Mijares Torres

item.title: Belgium’s Premier Cancels Policy Speech Citing Budget Deadlock
item.description: Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever canceled a state of the union speech in parliament planned for Tuesday, citing a lack of agreement on the country’s budget within his government.
item.dc:creator: Max Ramsay

item.title: Deadly Attacks on Saudi Arabia Risk Wider War That Draws In US
item.description: This weekend’s deadly attacks on Riyadh’s main airport have demonstrated the ability of Yemen’s Houthis to strike at the heart of Saudi power, raising the risk of a dangerous escalation that could draw in the US.
item.dc:creator: Peter Martin and Simon Marks

item.title: Trump Says Russia and Ukraine Agreed to ‘Energy Ceasefire’
item.description: President Donald Trump said Sunday that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an “energy ceasefire” effective immediately.
item.dc:creator: Catherine Lucey and María Paula Mijares Torres
